name: Food in Your First Days
description: What you can eat early on, area by area: beach, desert, forest, snow and more.

pages.title: Food in Your First Days
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Hunt what lives nearby and cook it on a campfire.
- Wild crops and fruit are food in any season. Only replanting cares.
- Raw mushrooms aren't food: make stew.
- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Meat and fish don't quench thirst. Fruit does.

Food is spread thin here: lots of species, each in its own biome. This entry lists what is **easy to get with stone tools, a crafting table and a campfire**, area by area.\
\
Each area page starts with the best options. Rare finds are marked as such.

pages.title: Seasons
pages.text:
The world starts in **early spring**. A wild crop you pick is food straight away; the season only matters when you plant it.\
\
In season now: carrots, potatoes, onions, sweet berries and strawberries.\
Wheat is a summer crop, so seeds from grass grow slowly until then. See [#](2E5AAC)[Seasonal Crops](entry://survival/seasons_crops)[#]().

pages.title: Your kitchen
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Campfire:** 3 sticks, coal or charcoal, 3 logs. No coal? Smelt a log in a furnace for charcoal.\
\
It cooks 4 things at once with no fuel, boils water and keeps you warm.\
\
Bowls: 3 planks make 4.

pages.title: Board and knife
pages.text: A **Cutting Board** (4 planks, 2 sticks) and a **Flint Knife** (flint, stick) slice pineapples, melons and pumpkins and cut meat. The Cooking Pot needs iron, so it comes later.

pages.title: Everywhere
pages.text:
- **Grass** drops wheat seeds, and short grass also coffee beans and cassava seeds. All three are summer crops.
- **Oak leaves** drop apples (rare) and acorns.
- **Mushroom stew:** a brown and a red mushroom in a bowl, on a crafting table.
- **Zombies** sometimes drop onions.

pages.title: Fishing
pages.text:
A rod is 3 sticks and 2 string. Hold to cast; when a fish bites, click as the marker crosses the zone. Each biome has its own fish. Cook them on the campfire.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** pufferfish, lionfish, stonefish, blowfish, boxfish, hagfish and stingrays poison you raw.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Tip:** no rod? Aquaculture's fish swim in ponds and rivers. Hit one and it drops itself, edible even raw.\
\
Aquaculture's regional fish (piranha, halibut and the rest) bite on any rod now, in their own biomes. See [#](2E5AAC)[Fishing](entry://fishing/overview)[#]().

pages.title: Food that hydrates
pages.text:
Meat, fish, bread and potatoes give **no** water. Fruit does:

- **Best:** melon, pineapple slices, pears, peaches, oranges
- **Good:** apples, tomatoes, onions, mango
- **A little:** berries, carrots, beetroot

Melon juice (4 slices, sugar, bottle) is a full drink.

pages.title: Beach
pages.text:
- **Wild cabbages and beetroots** grow on the sand, about one patch every 30 chunks. Eat them as they are.
- **Pineapples:** cut one on the board for 6 slices, a top drink-food.
- **Wild rice** and **wild carrots and onions**, rarer.
- **Crabs:** a claw becomes Raw Crab in the crafting grid.

No cows, pigs or sheep spawn on beaches; fish and crabs are your meat. Dried kelp (smelt kelp) is weak but endless.\
\
**Stony shore:** wild potatoes and crabs.\
**Snowy beach:** cabbages and beetroots too.

pages.title: Beach food
pages.text: Wild cabbages, pineapples and crabs. Cabbage and beetroot are autumn crops, so they grow slowly if you plant them in spring.

pages.title: Ocean and river
pages.text:
- **Fish** with a rod, or hit Aquaculture fish swimming by.
- **Clams** (Naturalist) on the sea floor give Clam Meat.
- **Squid** killed with a knife drop tentacles.
- **Rivers:** ducks, bass, crayfish and salmon.

Running river water is one step cleaner than still water.

pages.title: Desert
pages.text:
- **Rabbits** are the easy meat. **Komodo dragons** drop bushmeat but bite back.
- **Hamimelons** (Fruits Delight) grow only here: break one for slices.
- **Wild tomatoes** are rare and give few tomatoes.
- **Desert villages**: wheat farms, water and bread in chests.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Tip:** deserts count as tropical, so **summer crops grow all year**: wheat, melons, tomatoes, sugar cane. Spring and autumn crops grow slowly here.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** it never rains in a desert. Carry water.

pages.title: Badlands
pages.text: The thinnest area for food: wild tomatoes, komodo dragons, rabbits on the edges and whatever you can fish. Summer crops grow all year, so build the farm early or move on.

pages.title: Savanna
pages.text:
**No cows, pigs, sheep or chickens** spawn here. Instead:

- **Ostriches:** drumsticks, the best meat here
- **Boars:** porkchops
- **Hippos:** melon slices, but they hit hard
- **Giraffes and elephants:** bushmeat

Avoid lions. Summer crops grow all year.

pages.title: Jungle
pages.text:
The richest start:

- **Melons** grow wild, lots of them
- **Pigs, cows, sheep, chickens** and **capybaras** (bushmeat)
- **Wild rice**, cranberry bushes and fruit trees: mango, peach, lychee, durian

Summer crops grow all year. Rice needs the Cooking Pot.

pages.title: Plains and meadow
pages.text:
- **Plains:** cows, sheep, pigs and chickens. Hedgehogs, rats and snakes drop morsels.
- **Wild carrots and onions**, about one patch per 120 chunks.
- **Lemon trees** (one per 32 chunks) and rare blueberry and raspberry bushes.
- **Villages:** bread, potatoes, carrots, farms.
**Meadow** has few animals: some sheep and rabbits, and hedgehogs. Look for lemon trees, carrots and onions, or head to a plains village.

pages.title: Forests
pages.text:
No pigs in forests. Instead:

- **Deer** (venison), **boars** (porkchops), **turkeys** (drumsticks), plus cows, sheep, chickens
- **Fruit trees** in forest and flower forest, about 1 in 20 chunks: apple, orange, fig, kiwi
- **Pear trees** in birch forest, 1 in 15 chunks

**Dark forest:** cranberry bushes, and the huge mushrooms drop mushrooms for stew. Lots of monsters at night.\
\
**Cherry grove:** the weakest spot. Deer are the main meat, with a few rabbits and sheep.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** bears and tigers drop no food. Leave them alone.

pages.title: Forest food
pages.text: Venison, drumsticks and wild fruit. Cook meat on the campfire: cooked venison and drumsticks fill 6.

pages.title: Taiga
pages.text:
One of the best starts:

- **Sweet berries**, common and in season
- **Brown mushrooms** everywhere (red ones are rarer)
- **Turkeys**, cows, sheep, pigs, rabbits
- **Wild potatoes**, hawberry trees, blueberry bushes

Bears here are dangerous and drop only fur.

pages.title: Snow
pages.text:
**Snowy plains, snowy taiga, ice spikes:** rabbits, persimmon trees, blueberry bushes, rare sweet berries, and fish (break the ice).\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() Snowy biomes grow only **winter crops**: cabbage, sweet berries, hawberry, kiwi, persimmon.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() Set up the campfire first: it cooks and warms you at once. When you are too cold, part of your hearts freeze and won't heal, so food alone can't patch you up. See [#](2E5AAC)[Temperature](entry://survival/temperature)[#]().

pages.title: Mountains
pages.text:
- **Grove:** deer, boars, persimmon trees.
- **Slopes and peaks:** goats (they drop chevon), rabbits on the slopes. Mammoths have lots of meat but fight hard.
- **Stony peaks:** wild tomatoes.
- **Windswept hills:** like plains, plus wild potatoes.

pages.title: Swamp and mangrove
pages.text:
**No cows, pigs, sheep or chickens.** Instead:

- **Ducks**, **bass**, **catfish** and **capybaras**
- **Wild rice**, blueberry and cranberry bushes
- **Mushrooms**, both colors, for stew

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() Swamp water is Dirty: boil it.

pages.title: Mushroom fields
pages.text: **Mooshrooms** drop beef, and milking one with a bowl gives mushroom stew. Fungi Delight's morel and inky cap cows drop beef too. Mushrooms are everywhere.

pages.title: Caves
pages.text:
- **Lush caves:** glow berries hang from the ceiling, lots of them, all year. They hydrate a little.
- **Alex's Caves' Candy Cavity** is full of sweets, but it's deep and dangerous. Not a day-one trip.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** Terralith biomes work like the closest vanilla area: a Terralith desert follows the desert page, and so on.\
\
**MushroomQuest** stumps and logs in forests, taigas and swamps drop dozens of wild mushrooms. Some are good food, some are deadly. Read the tooltip before you eat one.

Fungi Delight's **morels** and **inky caps** aren't food raw. Inky caps cut on the board into cleaned caps; morels go into Cooking Pot dishes.\
\
Patch rarity: wild cabbages and beetroots 1 in 30 chunks, wild rice 1 in 20, carrots and onions 1 in 120, potatoes and tomatoes 1 in 100.
